question.text: Which of these Cat III strategies is GENERALLY expected to have the LOWEST volatility (annualised standard deviation) in a well-constructed book?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, market-neutral strategy minimises systematic risk by maintaining a zero or close-to-zero beta through balanced long/short pairs, which makes it the lowest-volatility Cat III strategy among the options shown. The Trap: Dedicated-long, short-bias, and leveraged global-macro carry directional or leveraged exposure, so they show higher volatility than market-neutral. Note: The workbook cautions that a zero beta does not eliminate volatility entirely — market-neutral books can still have idiosyncratic and tail risk even though systematic risk is minimised.
